subject: Post-charge mediation: August capacity spike and remediation
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@greensys.io>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenSys Billing <billing@greensys.io>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unplanned post-term charge for August spike

Hi David,

We just received the August invoice and there is a sizable one-time charge (~$46k) labeled as a post-term capacity adjustment. This spike is unexpected — our engineering team found a deployment bug that routed retries into a live inference pool for ~36 hours on 8/22-8/23, which inflated token counts.

Can you review the usage and the charge? From our side we can share the request logs and a short summary (attached). We want to understand options for mitigation: either an amortized payment schedule or a one-time goodwill reduction while we work through procurement.

Attached: greensys_spike_logs.csv (sample request ids and timestamps).

I can be available for a 30m call tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Anjali Rao
Finance Operations
GreenSys, Inc.
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@greensys.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unplanned post-term charge for August spike

Anjali — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I pulled the invoice and the usage window you called out lines up with a sharp increase in request volume.

We absolutely want to work this through. High level options we typically offer:
- Evidence-based credit: if the spike is attributable to an obvious bug and you provide logs, we can apply a one-time credit (partial) and amortize the remainder across the next 2-3 invoices.
- Fixed amortization: Redwood can defer the charge into 3 monthly installments and waive any late fees while you process procurement.

I'll loop in Ben (account lead) and Laura (billing) to put concrete numbers and a proposal on the table. Can you also share the PO number or purchase path — procurement often speeds acceptance when we include the right docs.

I copied your original below. Happy to do a quick call tomorrow afternoon.

—David

On Thu, Sep 10, 2026 at 11:14 AM Anjali Rao <anjali@greensys.io> wrote:
> Hi David,
>
> We just received the August invoice and there is a sizable one-time charge (~$46k) labeled as a post-term capacity adjustment...
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 12:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unplanned post-term charge for August spike (GreenSys)

Folks — forwarding Greensys' note. Quick summary: they have a 36-hour spike tied to a deployment bug. They attached sample logs. They are on an annual committed plan (DL-9347) and this is a post-term ad-hoc charge.

My proposed approach: validate the logs, then offer either (a) 40% one-time credit + amortize remaining 60% over 3 invoices, or (b) full amortization over 3 invoices with a 25% goodwill credit if procurement signs within 14 days. Either path waives late fees and includes a short post-mortem from GreenSys.

I've sketched the amortization options in the attached draft. If you agree, Ben can send the official proposal to Anjali and cc Laura for billing adjustments.

Attachments: redwood_draft_amortization.pdf

-David
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@greensys.io>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal for August adjustment — GreenSys (DL-9347)

Hi Anjali — thanks for sharing the logs and for your patience. We reviewed the usage with Billing and Engineering.

Proposal (pick one):
1) Goodwill + amortize: Redwood applies a 40% credit to the one-time charge. The remaining balance will be split equally across your next three monthly invoices (no interest, no late fees).
2) Full amortization + expedited sign: Redwood amortizes the full charge across 3 months and applies an additional 15% credit if procurement returns the signed amendment within 14 days.

Practical stuff: we can issue an adjusted invoice for September reflecting the credit (attached) and create the amortization entries for October/November. If you prefer a single credit to close this out, let us know and we will route for approvals.

Attachments: invoice_202609.pdf (the invoice with the 40% credit line item)

Next step: please confirm which option you prefer by EOD Monday (9/14) and, if possible, provide the PO or procurement contact. If helpful, we can also do a 20m call today to walk through numbers.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@greensys.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal for August adjustment — GreenSys (DL-9347)

Ben — appreciate the quick review and the options. Given the impact to our budget from the unexpected charge, GreenSys accepts option (1) — the 40% goodwill credit + 3-month amortization of the remainder. We will route the amendment through procurement immediately and expect to provide a PO by next week.

Two asks before we finalize:
- Can Redwood confirm in writing that no late fees or collection actions will be taken while amortization is active?
- Please include a short line in the amendment that the credit is contingent on the post-mortem demonstrating the burst was accidental (our engineers can produce a 2-page summary).

If you can send the updated amendment and adjusted invoice, I will get procurement to prioritize. Thanks for working with us on this.

Best,
Anjali
Finance Operations
GreenSys, Inc.
